item.title: CKB Talk Daily Brief - 2026-10-04

item.title: A Revenue Layer for CKB Nodes (3 posts)
item.description: Thanks all. Answering the last three together. I’m also updating the first post to reflect where this thread has taken the idea. Corrected parts are struck through, not deleted, so the history stays visible. Where this came from. The trigger was a concrete need: CRT needs many independent nodes to hold key shares and release them when the conditions are met. Rather than recruit a separate network just for CRT, I asked whether CKB node operators could run it. The idea is generic: the same runner could host CRT, CrowdCell’s finalization bot, and any app that today depends on one server of its own. @janx Agreed, a separate project. item.title: 分享一个 Tinder 版预测市场应用的想法 (1 posts)
item.description: Hi Fisher, I think this is technically feasible now. With CKB handling the market state / settlement and Fiber providing the micropayment layer, most of the primitives needed for this kind of high-frequency, small-value interaction are already there. The bigger issue, in my view, is no longer implementation but liquidity bootstrapping, especially the initial LP depth for each market. A Tinder-like UX potentially creates a very large number of small markets, so liquidity can become fragmented very quickly. Even if the protocol has reasonable total TVL, each individual card may still be too shallow to provide a meaningful price or smooth entry/exit. This can partly be avoided with pari-...

item.title: Lineage: working through batch release evidence with CellScript (1 posts)
item.description: I started building this after discussing the idea with a mate who works in pharma. As the author of CellScript, I kept coming back to the same question: When a batch becomes “released,” what exactly did someone approve—and can another participant check it without asking the original application for its verdict? I built Lineage to work through that question. It follows a batch through evidence collection, quality review, release, and a later correction. There is a working interface, signed records, an export you can verify offline, and a release predicate executed locally in CKB-VM through CellScript. item.title: Introducing a Stealth Address Extension for CCC (2 posts)
item.description: Nice work. I did something with stealth addresses in the past on wraith protocol: Wraith Protocol: Stealth Address Payments on CKB Nice to see this on CCC. Thanks! I actually came across Wraith Protocol while researching the existing stealth-address work on CKB. It’s great to see another implementation of the idea. My focus now is exploring how this can fit naturally into CCC and make the experience easier for applications to adopt.

item.title: CKB Script Port: testing state transfer between light clients (1 posts)
item.description: I’ve been working on a small experiment called CKB Script Port. The idea is to see whether already-synced state for one CKB Script can be moved from one light-client installation to another, so the new installation does not always have to rebuild the same Script history from scratch. I first tested this with Pocket Node, and later with iBytes. While testing the iBytes setup, I ran into an interesting light-client case. A Script can be synced up to a certain block height even when the light-client database does not have the exact block hash for that height stored locally.
